title: Labour Of Love with Martin Freeman & Tamsin Greig - Review
transcript: labor of love don't be put off by the labor part of the title of this wonderful comedy by James Graham because really it's about love it's a love letter to the Labour Party it's also about the way in which the two factions the modernizers and the traditionalists love the party and maybe need each other and even perhaps love each other a bit the two factions are represented by a labor MP Martin Freeman and his agent Tamsin Greig I love them the chemistry between them is wonderful riding may have Benedict and Beatrice in much ado about nothing but they're not just ciphers you really feel their joy and their pain whenever they're together by themselves this place sizzles the temperature drops a bit when other characters more stereotypes come on but still this is a very funny play it's also very clever it starts at the last election then takes us back through a series of scenes to the time of Kinnick then in act 2 we go forward again but this time we perceive things a little bit differently because we're seeing them backwards which is something of the theme of the play and indeed the outcome of the play I give it four stars you
